what: What happened that we did NOT forecast, and that a detector frozen beforehand caught. This is the opposite of FORECAST_LEDGER.json and is kept for the opposite reason.

difference.FORECAST_LEDGER: what did we predict, and were we right?
difference.SURPRISE_LEDGER: what moved outside its own history, when did our detector see it, and what did we later learn it was?

rules: an entry is created ONLY by a detector that was frozen before the period it fired on. A detector invented after seeing a shift may never create an entry, retroactively or otherwise.
the explanation field is filled AFTER the signal, never before. Searching for a trend that suits a known event is how a repository starts telling stories.
a signal that later reverses stays in the ledger with its reversal recorded. False alarms are the point of keeping the file.
interpretation_status begins UNEXPLAINED and may stay there permanently.

schema.detector_version: commit and contract parameters at fire time
schema.confirmation_period: hijri quarter, or null if never confirmed
schema.baseline_expectation: median and spread at fire time
schema.interpretation_status: UNEXPLAINED | PUBLICATION_ARTEFACT | COMPOSITION_SHIFT | LEGAL_CHANGE | PARSER_ERA | REVERSED

prospectiveEntriesNote: EMPTY, and correctly so. Every detector in this repository was frozen today. Nothing can yet have fired prospectively, and the historical replay below is NOT a set of surprises: those quarters were in the past when the detector was written.

historicalReplayForCalibration.purpose: to measure how often the frozen rules fire on ordinary quarters, not to claim any discovery

positiveControl.event: the Civil Transactions Law becoming citable
positiveControl.whyItQualifies: its date is fixed by legislation, not chosen by us after seeing the series, so it is definable without hindsight
positiveControl.limit: one positive control is one positive control. It shows the detector can fire on a real structural change; it does not establish sensitivity.
